To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) traditional healers are seen by students as being less credible than health professionals, but (ii) this is not associated with a belief in the credibility or otherwise of health professionals.
(1) the average credibility ratings of traditional healers are lower than those of modern health professionals, but (2) the credibility ratings of the two groups are not correlated.
In Malawi, a pluralistic (traditional and modern together) approach to AIDS prevention was judged to be credible by a majority of students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of traditional healers in the prevention of AIDS in sub-Saharan Africa.
the role of pluralism in the management of the AIDS crisis in Malawi.
the credibility of modern and traditional healers in the management of AIDS in Malawi, Africa, and the potential for a pluralistic approach in the management of this crisis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pluralism of traditional and modern medicine is a desirable goal in the prevention of AIDS, and that it is possible to achieve this goal without compromising the credibility of modern medical practitioners.

the credibility of modern and traditional health workers are not necessarily related to each other and therefore, in the case of AIDS, there is no reason to exclude either from the health care system.
the credibility of traditional healors is not a significant predictor of the credibility of modern medical professionals in the context of the AIDS crisis in Malawi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in Africa, pluralistic health care is a viable option for AIDS management.
a pluralistic approach is a viable option for the prevention of AIDS in Malawi, and probably elsewhere in Africa.
the pluralist model of health service provision is the most effective way to manage AIDS and other health problems in many African communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the credibility of modern and traditional healers should not be seen as a zero-sum game.
the AIDS crisis in Malawi and elsewhere should not be managed by a single approach.
the AIDS epidemic in Africa should not be managed as a "medical" problem.
